toegepas.blok: Genoeg, en nie te veel nie
toegepas.voor: Elke groep êrens op jou bord beteken nog nie balans nie.
toegepas.na: As elke groep êrens op jou bord is, beteken dit nog nie balans nie.
toegepas.rede_vinder: A noun phrase with a place adverbial as subject of 'beteken' is wooden; a conditional clause reads naturally.
toegepas.fout: A noun phrase with a place adverbial as subject of 'beteken' is wooden and makes the reader stumble.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The conditional clause is what a fluent writer would write and says exactly the same thing.

toegepas.blok: Genoeg, en nie te veel nie
toegepas.voor: het kos nodig om mee te bou
toegepas.na: het kos nodig om sy liggaam mee te bou
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'om mee te bou' leaves the object of building vague; naming the body makes the clause complete without adding content.
toegepas.fout: 'om mee te bou' leaves the clause without an object and reads as incomplete.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Naming the body only makes explicit what the sentence already means, and 'sy' follows the previous sentence's 'sy ouderdom'.

toegepas.voor: Met 'n vrug en groente by is al vier groepe daar.
toegepas.na: As hy ook 'n vrug en groente eet, is al vier groepe daar.
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Met ... by is' is clumsy; a conditional clause with Thabo as subject is more natural and keeps the meaning.
toegepas.fout: 'Met 'n vrug en groente by is' is a clumsy construction for a Grade 6 reader.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The conditional with Thabo as subject reads naturally and keeps the same condition and result.

laat_vaar.blok: Vier groepe, plus water en vesel
laat_vaar.voor: gee energie, en vette en olies soos botter ook.
laat_vaar.na: gee energie. Vette en olies soos botter gee ook energie.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The elliptical second half ('en vette en olies soos botter ook') has no verb, so the comma before 'en' does not follow the AWS rule; two complete sentences are clearer for Grade 6.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The elliptical 'en vette en olies soos botter ook' is natural Afrikaans with its own subject; splitting it lengthens the block and repeats 'energie' without making it clearer.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'die oorskot' names the extra energy precisely; 'die res' can read as the rest of the food.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'die res' clearly refers to the energy not used; 'oorskot' is a lateral and slightly harder word.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: After 'sonder', 'enigiets' is the idiomatic indefinite; 'van iets' sounds like a specific unnamed thing.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'sonder te veel van iets' is acceptable, it is a glossary definition, and the change would break the parallel with the 'swak dieet' definition's 'te veel van iets'.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: A condition one is in takes 'waarin'; 'waarby' is less idiomatic with 'toestand'.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'n Toestand waarby' is standard Afrikaans medical phrasing and matches the diabetes definition's 'waarby'; a lateral change to a glossary definition.

laat_vaar.na: Skade wat die suur van kieme
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The subject 'suur van kieme' needs the article to read as a clear noun phrase.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'suur' is a mass noun and grammatical without the article, and 'die suur' in a glossary entry read alone points back to an acid not mentioned.

vlae.blok: Vier groepe, plus water en vesel
vlae.teks: Vitamiene en minerale uit vars vrugte en groente help jou gesond bly.
vlae.rede: Not a safety flag and not a language change: a protected entry says the lesson must not suggest vitamins and minerals come only from fruit and vegetables; this sentence names only that source, which a checker may want to look at. Left unchanged because fixing it would alter content.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: A disease 'kom' is colloquial; 'ontstaan' is the written form and matches the lesson's own 'kan deels uit 'n swak dieet ontstaan'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'skeurbuik kom as' is plain, natural Afrikaans for a Grade 6 reader and matches the glossary; 'ontstaan' is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: As a conjunction introducing a clause, written Afrikaans uses 'totdat' rather than 'tot'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'tot' is an accepted conjunction in Afrikaans, so this is no grammar error and a glossary definition is not reworded for style.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Ontstaan' is the written form for a disease arising; keeps the glossary consistent with the study text if that change is kept.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'kom as' is acceptable plain wording, and a glossary definition is not reworded for style; the consistency argument falls away with change 7 dropped.

laat_vaar_vorige.na: en kry nie hulle vitamien C nie
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'mis' in the sense of 'miss out on' follows English; 'kry nie ... nie' is the natural Afrikaans for not getting something.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'mis' in the sense of going without is ordinary Afrikaans, and the proposal adds a word at the ceiling and stacks a second 'nie ... nie' right after 'geen ... nie', making the sentence heavier.
